text:
talia: quick note from the handoff soak: we see a small class of prefixes that end up in the "sticky orphan pool" after a lease-release + enqueue retry race. memory creeps and p95 token latency blips. logs below.

ben: can you paste a minimal trace?

talia: sure:
[lease] release prefix=team/zen/42 epoch=918 -> OK
[evict] enqueue prefix=team/zen/42 tag=hot id=0xdead -> ENQUEUED owner=old-007
[lease] release retry prefix=team/zen/42 epoch=918 -> OK (retry)
[evict] enqueue prefix=team/zen/42 id=0xdead -> dedupe: already-present (no ack)
[new-owner] bind shard=12 epoch=919 -> ok
[evict] dequeue id=0xdead -> lookup failed (owner-key mismatch)

ow the entry sits in queue but no one can address it.

owen: hmm classic ack-window leakage. two layers of possible fixes: 1) short-term: make release block for a small bounded time waiting for enqueue ack (e.g., 200ms) then fall back async and emit release_fallback metric; 2) short-term alternative: best-effort reconciler that scans for entries whose owner mapping mismatches and tries to remap or mark for TTL; 3) long-term: remove owner-bound index and switch to stable global enqueue-id (prefix+enqueue-uuid) with CAS-based dedupe.

li: adding to that: tombstone semantics are tricky. tombstone messages must always be able to remove queue entries even across epochs, but we should prevent old tombstones from resurrecting. proposal: tombstone carries tombstone_epoch and tombstone_id; dequeue applies tombstone only if tombstone_epoch >= entry.origin_epoch.

ben: tradeoffs: 1 (release-wait) is quickest to ship and fixes most races but increases latency on release RPCs. 2 (reconciler) is least invasive but eventual and heavy at scale if done aggressively. 3 (stable-id) is the cleanest correctness-wise but requires schema change, CAS on enqueue, and a careful migration (dual-write window + backfill).

talia: operational mitigation plan: enable release-wait behind a flag on one canary shard (200ms), add metrics: release_fallback_count, enqueue_dedupe_hits, orphaned_queue_entries; also enable a low-rate reconciler (1% QPS) to sweep obvious mismatches.

owen: also think about making enqueue ack idempotent and durable: currently dedupe uses in-memory set per coordinator. If we store origin_epoch and origin_owner in the queue row and make enqueue a conditional write keyed on (prefix, id) that returns the current row, retries can observe a stable state. That helps reconcile old retries.

li: for the long-term RFC: include schema for a stable enqueue key (fields: enqueue_uuid, origin_epoch, tombstone_flag, origin_owner), CAS semantics, migration steps (dual-write then cutover), GC for stale enqueue_uuid, benchmarks for CAS enqueue latency and conflict rate. Also include a chaos test plan (concurrent releases + handoffs + delayed retries).

ben: ops checklist for canary: feature flag, dashboards for the metrics talia listed, rollback steps (disable flag + accelerate reconciler TTL to prune), postmortem trigger if orphaned_queue_entries > 500 for 10m.

talia: I'll open the PR with release-wait + low-rate reconciler and the smoke tests. tagging reviewers. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: ack-window-mitigation.v1 -> canary-5 at 2026-03-24T03:00:00Z

owen: one more note: make sure reconciler logs the enqueue_uuid and any attempted remap so we can audit any deletions. Also emit an operator event when the reconciler actually reassigns or deletes an entry.

li: agree. and add a metric for reconciler_action_count broken down by action_type (remap, delete, noop).

ben: if canary is green we can iterate on stable-id RFC and schedule the migration runway.

talia: thanks everyone. PR incoming.
